blocks.text: 86 שַׁחֲרִית לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 86
uncertainties: The header is printed small and faint. I couldn't see the pointing clearly enough to verify it, so it may not exactly match the image.

blocks.text: וּבְנוֹתֵיהֶם וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָהֶם. וּמִי שֶׁמְּיַחֲדִים בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת לִתְפִלָּה. וּמִי שֶׁבָּאִים בְּתוֹכָם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל. וּמִי שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים נֵר לַמָּאוֹר וְיַיִן לְקִדּוּשׁ וּלְהַבְדָּלָה וּפַת לָאוֹרְחִים וּצְדָקָה לַעֲנִיִּים. וְכָל־מִי שֶׁעוֹסְקִים בְּצָרְכֵי צִבּוּר בֶּאֱמוּנָה. הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יְשַׁלֵּם שְׂכָרָם וְיָסִיר מֵהֶם כָּל־מַחֲלָה וְיִרְפָּא לְכָל־גּוּפָם וְיִסְלַח לְכָל־עֲוֹנָם וְיִשְׁלַח בְּרָכָה וְהַצְלָחָה בְּכָל־מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם עִם כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲחֵיהֶם. וְנֹאמַר אָמֵן:
uncertainties: This picks up mid-prayer from the previous page. The earlier part is not on this scan.
כְנֵסִיּוֹת: I can't tell whether the kaf has a dagesh. It looks like it doesn't.
לָאוֹרְחִים: the vowel under the lamed looks like qamats, but it might be shva or patah.
לַעֲנִיִּים: the lamed has patah, and there may also be a meteg.

blocks.text: הַנּוֹתֵן תְּשׁוּעָה לַמְּלָכִים וּמֶמְשָׁלָה לַנְּסִיכִים. מַלְכוּתוֹ מַלְכוּת כָּל־עוֹלָמִים. הַפּוֹצֶה אֶת־דָּוִד עַבְדּוֹ מֵחֶרֶב רָעָה. הַנּוֹתֵן בַּיָּם דֶּרֶךְ וּבְמַיִם עַזִּים נְתִיבָה. הוּא יְבָרֵךְ וְיִשְׁמוֹר וְיִנְצוֹר וְיַעֲזוֹר וִירוֹמֵם וִיגַדֵּל וִינַשֵּׂא לְמַעְלָה אֶת אֲדוֹנֵנוּ פלוני יָרוּם הוֹדוֹ: מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים בְּרַחֲמָיו יְחַיֵּהוּ וְיִשְׁמְרֵהוּ וּמִכָּל־צָרָה וְיָגוֹן וָנֶזֶק יַצִּילֵהוּ. וְיַדְבֵּר עַמִּים תַּחַת רַגְלָיו וְיַפִּיל שׂוֹנְאָיו לְפָנָיו וּבְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יִפְנֶה יַצְלִיחַ. מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים בְּרַחֲמָיו יִתֵּן בְּלִבּוֹ וּבְלֵב כָּל־יוֹעֲצָיו וְשָׂרָיו רַחֲמָנוּת לַעֲשׂוֹת טוֹבָה עִמָּנוּ וְעִם כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל. בְּיָמָיו וּבְיָמֵינוּ תִּוָּשַׁע יְהוּדָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל יִשְׁכֹּן לָבֶטַח וּבָא לְצִיּוֹן גּוֹאֵל. וְכֵן יְהִי רָצוֹן. וְנֹאמַר אָמֵן:
uncertainties: פלוני is printed small and without vowels at the end of the line, after אֲדוֹנֵנוּ. It is a placeholder where the reader inserts the ruler's name. I kept it in the text, but it could also be treated as a small inline direction.
After עוֹלָמִים there are two dots ('..'). This is probably a printing flaw, and I wrote it as one period.
וְיַעֲזוֹר and the first word of the paragraph may have a meteg that I couldn't confirm.
The prayer text is printed smaller than the paragraph above. I checked the small vowel marks against the enlarged strips, but some may still be wrong.

blocks.text: 86 Morning Prayer for the New Year 86

and all that belong to them; those who set aside synagogues for prayer and those who come to pray in them; those who provide light for illumination, wine for Kiddush and Havdalah, bread for strangers, charity for the poor; and all those who occupy themselves faithfully with the affairs of the community. May the Holy One, blessed be He, pay their reward, avert from them all illness, heal all their body, forgive all their guilt and send blessing and success for all the work of their hands and that of all Israel, their brethren, and let us say: Amen.

May He who grants salvation to kings and dominion to princes, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, who delivered His servant David from the evil sword, who made a way through the sea, a path through mighty waters, bless, guard, protect, help, exalt, magnify and raise to grandeur our lord . . . May his majesty be exalted. May the King of kings in His mercy grant him life, guard him and deliver him from all adversity, grief and loss, subdue nations beneath his feet and overthrow his enemies before him and wherever he turns, may he be successful. May the King of kings lay in his heart and in the heart of all his advisers and princes compassion so as to deal kindly with us and all Israel. In his days and in ours may Judah be saved and Israel dwell in safety and may the Redeemer come to Zion, Thus may it be Thy will, and let us say: Amen.
uncertainties: The source prints a capital 'Thus' after a comma ('Zion, Thus'). I kept it as printed.

notes: I read both full pages and all four enlarged strips for s192. For s193 I read the full page and strip 2, which contains the Hebrew word that links the English to the Hebrew. The English page is clear at full resolution, so I didn't read s193 strips 1, 3 and 4.
Neither page has rubrics, Bible citations, sound sequences, Shabbat additions in brackets, German instructions, or footnotes. Both pages are blank at the bottom.
I found no cantillation marks on s192; the text has vowel points only.

Both pages are printed as page 86, as Hebrew and English facing pages. The Hebrew page has two paragraphs. The first, which continues from the previous page, is in larger type. The second, the prayer for the government, is in smaller type with its first line indented.
The English '. . .' after 'our lord' corresponds to the Hebrew placeholder פלוני.
